summary: Seiichi Mizuno worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kosaku Hamada at Kyoto University (~1925–1928, Litt.D. 1962), later serving there as a professor (1949–1968) and researcher at its Institute for Research in Humanities.

Seiichi Yagi is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) and later held positions at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono studied under Eiichi Makino, Daito Shimaji, Kanae Tada, and Jokan Chikazumi, graduating from the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1938–1951) and later at Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He later held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (~2005–2008), where he later served as an associate professor around 2012.

Seiji Nemoto specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at Meiji University (~1968–1978), he served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2004–2015).
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1968–1977) and Asia University (~1977–1987).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1987. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University around 2005.
Seikō Hirata studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. A Buddhist studies scholar, he held a post at Hanazono University from around 1954 to 1990.

Sein Tin was an author and scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1918–1922) under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927) and later completed studies at Christ Church, Oxford (~1927–1930).

Seiran Ouchi was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held a post at Nishi Hongan-ji and served as president of Toyo University (1914–1918). He also founded Hoshi Sodan in 1874 and Meikyo Shinshi in 1875.

Seiren Matsunami, who worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo (-1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. He held professorships at Kyushu University (attested 1965) and Rissho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including K. R. Norman, Ji Xianlin, and Oskar von Hinüber. He was professor and director at Soka University and served at IRIAB.

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), Taisho University (1940), and Toyo University (1952, 1955).
Seitatsu Matsunami was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and later as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto University under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he was a professor at Kyoto University (1976–1986) and Hanazono University.

Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1977 and 1990–1998).
Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and later served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1964).

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University from around 1964 to 1965.
